proposals.before: His great-great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
proposals.reason: 曾祖 denotes a great-grandfather (father's grandfather), not a great-great-grandfather.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
proposals.after: His grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
proposals.reason: 祖 in this genealogical sequence after 曾祖 denotes the grandfather, not the great-grandfather.

proposals.before: During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Military Commissioner Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.
proposals.after: During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.
proposals.reason: 監軍使 is an army-supervisor, not a jiedushi military commissioner.

proposals.before: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 is the Palace Library director, not the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Baron of a Founding State.
proposals.after: He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Viscount of a Founding State.
proposals.reason: 開國子 is a founding-fief viscount (子), not a baron (男).

proposals.before: His great-great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.
proposals.reason: Same kinship error as the idiomatic line: 曾祖 is great-grandfather.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.
proposals.after: His grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.
proposals.reason: 祖 here is grandfather, matching the Chinese genealogical generation.

proposals.before: Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yanzhou.
proposals.after: Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yunzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou is 兗州, which appears later as a different place.

proposals.before: Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yanzhou.
proposals.after: Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yunzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州).

proposals.before: When Youzhang governed Yanzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
proposals.after: When Youzhang governed Yunzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; the translation conflates it with Yanzhou.

proposals.before: Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yan by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.
proposals.after: Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yun by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州/鄆 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou/Yan (兗).

proposals.before: When Youzhang held Yanzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.
proposals.after: When Youzhang held Yunzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.

proposals.before: At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yan; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yan, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.
proposals.after: At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yun; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yun, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州/鄆 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou/Yan.

proposals.before: In the third year of Guanghua of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office robes he was appointed collator and served in remonstrance posts.
proposals.after: In the third year of Guanghua of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon doffing commoner's clothes (entering official service) he was appointed collator and served in remonstrance posts.
proposals.reason: 釋褐 means leaving commoner's clothing to take office, not leaving office robes.

proposals.before: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was praised for choosing worthy men; Chief Ministers Ma Yinsun and Pei Weihan were both jinshi he had advanced.
proposals.after: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was praised for choosing worthy men; Chief Ministers Ma Yinsun and Sang Weihan were both jinshi he had advanced.
proposals.reason: Chinese 維翰 is later called 桑公; the person is Sang Weihan (桑維翰), not a Pei.

proposals.before: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was said to have chosen worthy men; the chief ministers Ma Yinsun and Pei Weihan were both jinshi he had selected.
proposals.after: Hao repeatedly supervised the civil service examinations and was said to have chosen worthy men; the chief ministers Ma Yinsun and Sang Weihan were both jinshi he had selected.
proposals.reason: The same unit's 維翰 is Sang Weihan, as confirmed by 桑公 in s0102; Pei Weihan is a wrong surname.

proposals.before: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, he was promoted to vice director of the Revenue Department in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
proposals.after: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, he was promoted to vice director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
proposals.reason: 屯田員外郎 is the Agricultural Colonies (Tuntian) bureau of the Ministry of Works, not the Revenue Department (戶部).

proposals.before: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Revenue Department in the Ministry of Works and Drafter of Edicts.
proposals.after: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and Drafter of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 屯田員外郎 is the Agricultural Colonies bureau, not Revenue.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tianfu he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Secretariat drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianfu he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Secretariat drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
proposals.reason: 祠部郎中 is specifically the Bureau of Sacrifices, not a generic directorate of the Ministry of Rites.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tianfu he was changed to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as Director in the Ministry of Rites and Drafter of Edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianfu he was changed to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafter of Edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
proposals.reason: 祠部郎中 should be rendered as Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices.

proposals.before: At the start of the Tang Tianyou era he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then investigating censor at court. After three promotions he became vice director of the Bureau of Appointments and compiler in the History Office, then magistrate of Henan and director of the Ministry of Rites, received purple robes, and became right department director while also serving as censor-in-chief of miscellaneous affairs.
proposals.after: At the start of the Tang Tianyou era he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then investigating censor at court. After three promotions he became vice director of the Bureau of Appointments and compiler in the History Office, then magistrate of Henan and director of the Ministry of Rites, received purple robes, and became right department director while also serving as attending censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
proposals.reason: 侍御史知雜事 is an attendant censor managing miscellaneous censorate business, not the Censor-in-Chief (御史大夫).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office robes he was made collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then entered court as Investigating Censor. After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments, served as compiler in the History Office, was changed to magistrate of Henan and Director of the Ministry of Rites, was granted purple robes, and became Right Department Director concurrently Censor-in-Chief of Miscellaneous Affairs.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon doffing commoner's clothes he was made collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Jun Prefecture, then entered court as Investigating Censor. After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments, served as compiler in the History Office, was changed to magistrate of Henan and Director of the Ministry of Rites, was granted purple robes, and became Right Department Director concurrently Attending Censor in charge of Miscellaneous Affairs.
proposals.reason: 釋褐 means entering office from commoner status, not leaving office robes; 知雜事 is not Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers by Clan: Zhide was minister of war.)〉
proposals.after: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers by Clan: Zhide was minister of war.)
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English retains a stray Chinese annotation closer '〉' that is not part of the translated sentence.

proposals.before: Taoguang was a maternal grandson of Tang Emperor Xuanzong, born to Princess Wanshou. On the third day after his birth he was granted hereditary office status, with silver seal and crimson tassel.
proposals.after: Taoguang was a maternal grandson of Tang Emperor Xuanzong (Xuānzōng, 宣宗), born to Princess Wanshou. On the third day after his birth he was granted hereditary office status, with silver seal and crimson tassel.
proposals.reason: Chinese 唐宣宗 is Emperor Xuānzōng (宣宗, r. 846–859), not Emperor Xuánzōng (玄宗); the inherited spelling conflates the two temple names.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit, was posthumously honored as grand marshal with the posthumous title Weny, and has a biography in the Tang histories.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit, was posthumously honored as grand marshal with the posthumous title Wenyi, and has a biography in the Tang histories.
proposals.reason: The posthumous name 文懿 is Wenyi; 'Weny' drops the final syllable.

proposals.before: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou. An amnesty followed and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xuzhou.
proposals.after: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou. An amnesty followed and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture (modern Xuchang), not Xuzhou (徐州).

proposals.before: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was made director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was made director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 is the director of the Palace/Imperial Library, not the Secretariat (中書/尚書).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was changed to Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was changed to Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 does not mean Director of the Secretariat.

proposals.before: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year the court was at Ye. Yun suffered from gout and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.
proposals.after: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year the court was at Ye. Yun suffered from beriberi and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.
proposals.reason: 腳氣 is foot qi/beriberi, not gout (痛風).

proposals.before: Yi from youth could write; he passed the jinshi examination and upon leaving office robes was collator, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and assistant magistrate of Qinghe.
proposals.after: Yi from youth could write; he passed the jinshi examination and upon first donning official robes was collator, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and assistant magistrate of Qinghe.
proposals.reason: 解褐 means entering office for the first time (removing commoner's hemp), not leaving office robes.

decisions.reason: 曾祖 is the father's grandfather (great-grandfather). The genealogical sequence 曾祖 / 祖 / 父 confirms the original 'great-great-grandfather' is one generation too remote.
After 曾祖, 祖 names the grandfather. Rendering 祖宏慶 as great-grandfather collapses two generations.
監軍使 is an army supervisor, not a jiedushi (節度使) military commissioner.
秘書監 is director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat (中書).
開國子 is a founding-fief viscount (子); baron is 男.
The literal repeats the same 曾祖 error: Xiqi is Yao Yi's great-grandfather, not great-great-grandfather.
The literal likewise misreads 祖 as great-grandfather; in this sequence it is grandfather.
鄆州 is Yunzhou. Yanzhou is 兗州, which the chapter uses separately.
The literal has the same 鄆州/Yanzhou confusion; the place is Yunzhou.
友璋領鄆州 means he held Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.
襲據鄆州, 父母在鄆, and 歸鄆 all refer to Yunzhou, distinct from 兗州 in the previous unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 襲據鄆州……父母在鄆……歸鄆

decisions.reason: The literal repeats 鄆州 as Yanzhou; Youzhang held Yunzhou.
The literal likewise substitutes Yan for 鄆; the city and prefecture are Yunzhou.

decisions.after: In the third year of Guanghua of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon doffing commoner's clothes he was appointed collator and served in remonstrance posts.
decisions.reason: 釋褐 means doffing commoner's clothes to take office, not leaving official robes. The proposed parenthetical gloss is unnecessary in the literal line.
維翰 here is later called 桑公; the examinee is Sang Weihan, not a Pei.
The literal invents the surname Pei for 維翰; the chapter later names him 桑公.
尚書屯田員外郎 is vice director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau, not of the Revenue Department (戶部).
The literal makes the same 屯田/Revenue substitution.
祠部郎中 is director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, not a generic directorate of the Ministry of Rites (禮部郎中).
The literal likewise collapses 祠部郎中 into a Ministry of Rites directorate.
侍御史知雜事 is an attending censor managing miscellaneous Censorate business, not Censor-in-Chief (御史大夫).
釋褐 is entering office from commoner status, and 侍御史知雜事 is not Censor-in-Chief; both corrections match the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 釋褐除校書郎……兼侍御史知雜事

decisions.reason: The trailing 〉 is a leftover source-bracket closer, not part of the English sentence.

decisions.after: Taoguang was a maternal grandson of Tang Emperor Xuānzong, born to Princess Wanshou. On the third day after his birth he was granted hereditary office status, with silver seal and crimson tassel.
decisions.reason: 唐宣宗 is Xuānzong, not Xuanzong of the 712–756 reign. The proposal is right on identity but inserts Chinese 宣宗 into the English; the macron alone disambiguates.
謚曰文懿 is the posthumous name Wenyi; 'Weny' drops 懿.
許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not Xuzhou (徐州).
改秘書監 is director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.
The literal repeats the 秘書監/Secretariat error.
病腳氣 is foot qi/beriberi, not gout (痛風).
解褐 means first taking office by putting off commoner's hemp, not leaving official robes.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0015 shows 維翰 is Sang Weihan (later 桑公). The alternate name Pei Weihan was created solely by the mistranslation and has no source support.

claimRevisions.reason: The English title Military Commissioner was created by misreading 監軍使. The accepted repair restores Army Supervisor.
